output.brief: The departures are concentrated in one place: 8 of the 11 associates on the Kestrel matter have resigned, against 1 of 13 who were never on it. The rest of the firm, including the billable-target change, shows normal attrition, so a market-wide trend or the firm-wide target does not explain it. Kestrel work is the clear marker. The problem is that every Kestrel associate was also supervised by Dorian Faulk, and he supervises nobody else. So heavy workload and his supervision cannot be told apart in the records. Survey comments point to both (relentless weekends, and humiliating late-night corrections). Pay is mentioned but is not shown to be the cause. The exit forms are unreliable: leavers knew the practice head might see them, and they say little. I would not announce the £12k payment and close the review. It targets the weakest-supported explanation, and the group would be left with the cause untouched. Next steps: commission the outside confidential interviews (about £9k, three weeks), designed to separate supervision from workload. Add matter and supervising-partner fields to attrition tracking. Then choose between changing supervision, adding contract reviewers, or both. Kestrel moves to four associates in January, so the timing matters. I'm fairly sure the problem is Kestrel-specific, but not yet which part of it.
